title: Basic Classes of Functions
lead: Lines and their slope, polynomials and their end behavior and zeros, algebraic and transcendental functions, piecewise-defined functions, and the shifts, scalings and reflections that carry the graph of one function onto another: the basic classes of functions that calculus works with.
objectives: Calculate the slope of a linear function and interpret its meaning.
Recognize the degree of a polynomial.
Find the roots of a quadratic polynomial.
Describe the graphs of basic odd and even polynomial functions.
Describe the graphs of power and root functions.
Explain the difference between algebraic and transcendental functions.
Sketch the graph of a function that has been shifted, stretched, or reflected from its initial graph position.
summary_html:
• The power function $\kf(x)=x^{n}$ is an even function if $n$ is even and $n\ne 0,$ and it is an odd function if $n$ is odd.
  • The root function $\kf(x)=x^{1/n}$ has the domain $[0,\infty)$ if $n$ is even and the domain $(-\infty,\infty)$ if $n$ is odd. If $n$ is odd, then $\kf(x)=x^{1/n}$ is an odd function.
  • The domain of the rational function $\kf(x)=p(x)/q(x),$ where $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ are polynomial functions, is the set of $x$ such that $q(x)\ne 0.$
  • Functions that involve the basic operations of addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and powers are algebraic functions. All other functions are transcendental. Trigonometric, exponential, and logarithmic functions are examples of transcendental functions.
  • A polynomial function $\kf$ with degree $n\ge 1$ satisfies $\kf(x)\to\pm\infty$ as $x\to\pm\infty.$ The sign of the output as $x\to\infty$ depends on the sign of the leading coefficient only and on whether $n$ is even or odd.
  • Vertical and horizontal shifts, vertical and horizontal scalings, and reflections about the $x$- and $y$-axes are examples of transformations of functions.

exercises.prompt: Consider the line passing through points $(-3,2)$ and $(1,4).$ Find the slope of the line. Find an equation of that line in point-slope form. Find an equation of that line in slope-intercept form.

answer.solution: $m=1/2.$ The point-slope form is $y-4=\frac{1}{2}(x-1).$ The slope-intercept form is $y=\frac{1}{2}x+\frac{7}{2}.$

exercises.prompt: Consider the quadratic function $f(x)=3x^{2}-6x+2.$ Find the zeros of $f.$ Does the parabola open upward or downward?

answer.solution: The zeros are $x=1\pm\sqrt{3}/3.$ The parabola opens upward.

exercises.prompt: Find the domain and range for the function $f(x)=(5x+2)/(2x-1).$

answer.hint: The denominator cannot be zero. Solve the equation $y=(5x+2)/(2x-1)$ for $x$ to find the range.
answer.solution: The domain is the set of real numbers $x$ such that $x\ne 1/2.$ The range is the set $\{y\mid y\ne 5/2\}.$

exercises.prompt: Find the domain for each of the following functions: $f(x)=(5-2x)/(x^{2}+2)$ and $g(x)=\sqrt{5x-1}.$

answer.hint: Determine the values of $x$ when the expression in the denominator of $f$ is nonzero, and find the values of $x$ when the expression inside the radical of $g$ is nonnegative.
answer.solution: The domain of $f$ is $(-\infty,\infty).$ The domain of $g$ is $\{x\mid x\ge 1/5\}.$

exercises.prompt: Is $f(x)=x/2$ an algebraic or a transcendental function?

answer.solution: Algebraic

exercises.prompt: Sketch a graph of the function $$f(x)=\begin{cases}2-x, & x\le 2\\ x+2, & x\gt 2\end{cases}.$$

answer.hint: Graph one linear function for $x\le 2$ and then graph a different linear function for $x\gt 2.$

exercises.prompt: The cost of mailing a letter is a function of the weight of the letter. Suppose the cost of mailing a letter is 49¢ for the first ounce and 21¢ for each additional ounce. Write a piecewise-defined function describing the cost $C$ as a function of the weight $x$ for $0\lt x\le 3,$ where $C$ is measured in cents and $x$ is measured in ounces.

answer.hint: The piecewise-defined function is constant on the intervals $(0,1],(1,2],\ldots.$
answer.solution: $$C(x)=\begin{cases}49, & 0\lt x\le 1\\ 70, & 1\lt x\le 2\\ 91, & 2\lt x\le 3\end{cases}$$

exercises.prompt: Describe how the function $f(x)=-(x+1)^{2}-4$ can be graphed using the graph of $y=x^{2}$ and a sequence of transformations.

answer.solution: Shift the graph $y=x^{2}$ to the left 1 unit, reflect about the $x$-axis, then shift down 4 units.

exercises.prompt:
For the following exercises, determine whether the statement is true or false. Explain why.

$f(x)=(4x+1)/(7x-2)$ is a transcendental function.

answer.solution: False. $f(x)=(4x+1)/(7x-2)$ is a quotient of two polynomials, so it is a rational function, and a rational function is algebraic: it involves only basic algebraic operations. A transcendental function is one that cannot be described that way.

exercises.prompt:
For the following exercises, determine whether the statement is true or false. Explain why.

$g(x)=\sqrt[3]{x}$ is an odd root function

answer.solution: True; $n=3$

exercises.prompt:
For the following exercises, determine whether the statement is true or false. Explain why.

A logarithmic function is an algebraic function.

answer.solution: False. A logarithmic function $f(x)=\log_{b}(x)$ cannot be written with only the basic algebraic operations of addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, rational powers and roots, so it is transcendental; the logarithmic functions are among the most common transcendental functions.

exercises.prompt:

A function of the form $f(x)=x^{b},$ where $b$ is a real valued constant, is an exponential function.

answer.solution: False; $f(x)=x^{b},$ where $b$ is a real-valued constant, is a power function

exercises.prompt:
For the following exercises, determine whether the statement is true or false. Explain why.

The domain of an even root function is all real numbers.

answer.solution: False. For an even integer $n\ge 2,$ the root $x^{1/n}$ is not a real number when $x\lt 0,$ since no real number raised to an even power is negative. The domain of an even root function is $[0,\infty),$ not all real numbers.

exercises.prompt: [T] A company purchases some computer equipment for ＄20,500. At the end of a 3-year period, the value of the equipment has decreased linearly to ＄12,300. a. Find a function $y=V(t)$ that determines the value V of the equipment at the end of t years. b. Find and interpret the meaning of the $x$- and $y$-intercepts for this situation. c. What is the value of the equipment at the end of 5 years? d. When will the value of the equipment be ＄3000?

answer.solution: a. $V(t)=-2733t+20500$ b. $(0,20,500)$ means that the initial purchase price of the equipment is ＄20,500; $(7.5,0)$ means that in 7.5 years the computer equipment has no value. c. ＄6835 d. In approximately 6.4 years

exercises.prompt: [T] A family bakery makes cupcakes and sells them at local outdoor festivals. For a music festival, there is a fixed cost of ＄125 to set up a cupcake stand. The owner estimates that it costs ＄0.75 to make each cupcake. The owner is interested in determining the total cost $C$ as a function of number of cupcakes made. a. Find a linear function that relates cost C to x, the number of cupcakes made. b. Find the cost to bake 160 cupcakes. c. If the owner sells the cupcakes for ＄1.50 apiece, how many cupcakes does she need to sell to start making profit? (Hint: Use the INTERSECTION function on a calculator to find this number.)
[T] A car was purchased for ＄26,000. The value of the car depreciates by ＄1500 per year. a. Find a linear function that models the value V of the car after t years. b. Find and interpret $V(4).$

answer.solution: a. $V(t)=-1500t+26,000$ b. In 4 years, the value of the car is ＄20,000.
